title: On Ramsey number of $K_{2,n}$ versus even cycles
summary: For graphs $G$ and $H$, the Ramsey number $R(G,H)$ is the smallest integer $N$ such that every graph $Γ$ on $N$ vertices contains $G$ or its complement $\overlineΓ$ contains $H$ as a subgraph. In graph Ramsey theory, the star-cycle Ramsey number is well-studied throughout the years. Whereas the Ramsey number of $K_{2,n}$ versus cycle is challenging to determine due to increased structural complexity.
